request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** a search box (`search-name`) and a button (`search`) list every matching person over this sheet and the other sheets of its tree. Each match is a `search-line` reading `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`, and `search-count` shows how many there are.
- **Matching:** a person matches if the typed text appears anywhere in their name or one of their aliases, ignoring case. A blank search lists everyone.
- **Order:** this sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people by sheet id.
- **Due-total:** shown the way each person's own sheet shows it, using that sheet's today, rates, settings and floor. That's why Pam shows 1.00 rather than 0.10: the default floor of 1.00 applies.
- **Retired people** are included whether or not "show retired" is on.
- **Count:** it disappears while a search runs and reappears when it's done, so two identical searches can be told apart.

**Choices to check:**
- **What "tree" means.** The app already has two meanings. I used the one the "clashing" check uses: the sheet's ancestors and descendants. The other, used for claim numbering, is the top ancestor and every sheet under it, which would also pick up sibling and cousin sheets. The test can't tell them apart because its tree is a simple chain. If you meant the wider one, it's a one-line change in the new endpoint.
- **Live data.** The search reads every sheet from the store as it is now, even while the screen shows the sheet "as of" a date. That matches how the consolidated figures work.

**Changes:**
- `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree.GET.yml` and `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/RespondWithTree.java`: a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tree`. It reuses the existing `TreeNames.treeOf` and returns the other sheets' ids in id order.
- `src/main/frontend/features/people/search.slot.tsx`: the search box, button and results.

There are no database or audit changes, since a search writes nothing.

probe.probe_text:
I didn't change anything. Here is what I found after reading `ClaimFigures`, `Claim`, `ClaimStatus`, `ApplyClaimStatus`, `ClaimRules`, `Sheet`, `Period`/`ClosePeriod`, `Rollup`, `Person`, `TakeStatement` and the other step classes, plus the front-end feature slots and `rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `due.slot.tsx` and `periods.ts`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### A claim's row (`list.slot.tsx`)
- **`claim-number`**: given when the claim is opened (`ApplyClaimStatus`).
  - By default it is the next number in the fiscal year of its due-by, `FY<year>-<n>`, shared across the sheet's tree. The year starts in `fiscal-start-month`.
  - While `periodNumberingOn()` is true (`period-numbering-from` ≤ today), it is `<period>-<n>`, or `X-<n>` when the claim is in no period.
  - A voided claim keeps its number and numbers are never reused. A reassign or a split takes a new number; a transfer or clone takes the other sheet's next one.
- **`claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`**:
  - The amount has up to two decimals. A negative amount must name the settled claim it `corrects`, and only a negative amount may (`ClaimRules.check`).
  - A blank date takes `entryDateInForce()` (the entry date, else today) in `ClaimRules.make`. `ApplyClaim` (edit) uses `sheet.getToday()` instead.
  - When the claim has lines, its amount must equal the total of its lines.
- **`claim-due-by`**: `BusinessDays.after(dueFrom, dueTerms, holidays)`, skipping weekends and holidays.
  - Terms come from `Sheet.termsFor`: the person's own terms, else `terms-<grade>` in force on the date, else `terms` (default 14).
  - `dueFrom` and `dueTerms` are fixed when the claim is created. Re-dating or editing doesn't move them.
  - It is worked out again when a holiday is added, for claims that aren't SETTLED or VOID and whose due-by is on or after the new holiday (`ApplyHoliday`).
- **`claim-period`**: the period that contains the claim's **due-by**, not its date.
- **`claim-due`**: `ClaimFigures.due` on the server, and `chargedOf` in the front end. Its parts:
  - **The figure** (`figure`): the frozen `due` if the claim is settled; else `statedDue` if `isBound()` (stated and not PENDING); else the **live figure** (`liveFigure`).
  - **The live figure**: `amount × pct / 100`, where pct is the rate in force on the claim's date for the grade the person had on that date (`PersonGrades.on`).
    - Rates are looked up through `rateOn`: the latest from-date on or before the claim's date, dropped if `endedBy` (its to-date is before the date), then the parent sheets up the chain (`findInChain`). No rate means **n/a**.
  - **Rounding** (`rounding`): HALF_UP if `getRoundsOn()` is before `policyDateInForce()` (the policy date, else today), otherwise HALF_EVEN. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`correctsDate`).
  - **The late charge** (`lateCharge` / `chargeByBoundary`):
    - It applies only if the claim is `overdue` and is not a correction.
    - Lateness counts from `lateFrom` = due-by + `grace-<grade>` (the grade on the claim's date).
    - For each full 30 days up to today, it adds `latePctOn(boundary)` × (figure + earlier charges), compounding, each step rounded like the due. A 0.00 percent adds nothing.
  - **The floor** (`floored`) comes last: the result is at least `floorOn(claim date)` (default 1.00). A correction takes no floor.
  - A statement binds only the figure. The floor and the late charge keep following the sheet.
- **`claim-overdue`** (`overdue` / `isOverdue`): the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not `isDeferredOn(today)`, and `lateFrom` is before today.
- **`claim-stated`**: shows the raw `stated` flag, even while the claim is PENDING (when `isBound` is false).
- **`claim-deferred` / `claim-deferred-until`**: deferral works only on an OPEN claim, to a date after today (`ApplyDefer`).
  - While deferred, the claim counts nowhere, isn't overdue, can't be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound.
  - The UI flag shows the deferral whatever the claim's status.
- **The other row fields**:
  - `claim-proofs`: raised one at a time, but not on a SETTLED or VOID claim.
  - `claim-split-from`.
  - `claim-late-entry`: the claim was added while its due-by's period was soft-closed.
  - `claim-reminded`: one reminder per today, OPEN or PENDING only.
  - `claim-ref`: unique on the sheet, ignoring case.
  - `claim-tags`.
  - `claim-batch` (`settleBatch`).
  - `claim-opened-by`.
  - `claim-log`: `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`, written by `ClaimRules.log` with the due worked out at that moment.
  - `claim-void-reason`, comments, lines.

### Status rules (`ClaimStatus.after`, `ApplyClaimStatus.run`)
- **The flow**: DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED, with a branch through PENDING (approve → SETTLED, reject with a non-blank reason → OPEN). DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED → VOID, which is final. DRAFT → DELETED, which can be restored only on the today it was deleted (`log.deletedOn`).
- **Counting** (`counts`): only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count, and a deferred OPEN claim doesn't.
- **Who may act**:
  - `Sheet.allows(action, role)` applies the permission matrix (`perm-<action>`). The standing rule is that a clerk or steward may open, settle, void and close, and only a steward may reassign or reopen.
  - Roles are `clerk` (the default), `steward` and `viewer`. `GuardViewer` refuses every change by a viewer.
  - A `Delegation` makes a name act as steward between its dates.
  - `GuardArchived` refuses every change on an archived sheet. The as-of view refuses every change.
- **Settling and approving**:
  - The person who opened the claim (`openedBy`) can't settle or approve it, and neither can the person who last edited it (`editedBy`).
  - A deferred claim can't be settled.
  - If the due is above `proofThresholdFor(grade, date)` and the claim has no proofs, it's refused (`ProofRequiredException`). This is checked before the clerk limit.
  - If a non-steward settles a claim whose due is above `getClerkLimit()`, it goes PENDING. An n/a due is within any limit.
  - Settling fixes `due`. An n/a due stays live.
  - Only a steward may approve or reject.
- **Opening**:
  - A claim whose due is above `noteThresholdOn(date)` and has a blank note is refused.
  - If the due-by is in a period with a `cap`, opening is refused when the person already has `cap` OPEN or PENDING claims there.
- **Voiding a SETTLED claim**: steward only, within `VOID_DAYS = 7` of its settlement (`log.settledOn`). While the sheet has a list of void reasons, a void needs a reason from that list.
- **Closed periods**: no claim whose **due-by** falls in a closed period can be added, edited, locked, have lines added, change status, be deferred, re-dated, split, reassigned or re-settled.
- **Retirement**: a claim can't be dated after the person's `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement (`retiredOn`).
- **Editing**: only a DRAFT can be edited, and the editor lock (`lockedBy`) is checked by `GuardClaimLock`. A change of today releases all locks.
- **Re-dating** (`ApplyRedate`): steward only, OPEN or PENDING only. The due-by, number and any binding stay as they were.
- **Splitting** (`ApplySplit`): OPEN and not deferred, with 0 < split amount < the claim's amount. The original claim is unbound. The new claim gets a fresh due-by, a number and the late-entry flag.
- **Reassigning** (`ApplyReassign`): DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING only. The claim is renumbered, unbound, and relisted as the new person's newest claim.
- **Re-settling** (`ApplyResettle`): steward only, SETTLED only. It sets `due = openDue` (today's rates, grades, floor and charge, ignoring any binding).

### A person's row and the totals
- **`person-grade`**: the grade in force on today (`PersonGrades`). The first grade applies from the beginning of time; dated grades come from the form's from-date.
- **`person-claimed`**: the sum of the amounts of claims that pass `countsLive`, not counting corrections.
- **`countsLive`**: `counts`, minus the person's OPEN and PENDING **unbound** claims when `leftOn(date, today)` is true, meaning a hold covers the claim's date or `retiredBy(today)`.
- **`person-due-total`** (`ClaimFigures.dueTotal` / `personDue`):
  - It is the sum of `due` over the `countsLive` claims, or 0.00 when none count.
  - It is **n/a** when the grade on today has no rate on today, unless some counted claim is "kept": settled, bound with a figure, or live at another grade or dated on or before today with a figure.
  - It is capped at `getCap()`, the cap in force on today. n/a is never capped.
- **`person-excess`**: the sum before the cap, minus the cap.
- **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`**: counted overdue claims and the sum of their dues.
- **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`** (`split.slot.tsx`).
- **`person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60`, `-61`**: dues of OPEN and PENDING claims, bucketed by the claim's age in days.
- **`person-active`**: the person has a counted OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to today (`ACTIVE_DAYS`).
- **`person-backing`**: over the person's patrons, the sum of each patron's frozen dues on SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days (`BACKING_DAYS`), times that patron's share (`sharesOf`: an equal split rounded HALF_EVEN, with the remainder going to the first-named patron), rounded HALF_EVEN.
- **`person-period-<name>`**: the person's total for that period (see Periods).
- **`person-cut-total`**: the person's cuts in the pools (see Pools).
- **Statements** (`person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`):
  - `TakeStatement` records the due-total and binds every counted claim to its current figure. Claims that don't count are unbound.
  - A statement taken as of a date replays the sheet as of that date (`AsOf`). The date must be on or before today and not before the person's `addedOn`.
  - `CancelStatement` (steward only) unbinds the claims the last statement bound. It doesn't restore earlier bindings.
- **Holds, retirement and the rest**:
  - `person-hold`: a hold runs from a date (blank = today) to a date (blank = open-ended).
  - `person-retired-from`: a person with a date set counts as retired at once for refusals, but leaves the live totals only once today reaches the date.
  - Retirement lines, snapshot lines (`AuditSnapshot`: each person's due-total on the day being left when today changes).
  - Terms, contact, tags, aliases, origin, and `clashing` (`TreeNames`).

### Sheet-wide figures
- **`rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`**: everyone's figures added up.
- **`rollup-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`**: `trimmedSum`, which leaves out the single highest and lowest figure when there are three or more. n/a is skipped.
- **Header counters, `my-due-total`, `consolidated-*`, `search-line`**: other places that show due-totals or overdue-totals.
- **`month-<m>`, `tag-<t>`**: summed by the claim's date, and by its tag or its person's tag.
- **`summary-*`**: counts by grade, period, status and void reason.
- **The alert threshold**: a person crossing above it gets an `ALERT` record in the audit file. Nothing on screen shows it.

### Periods
- **`period-due-total` / `person-period-*`** (`ClosePeriod.totals`, `periodDue`):
  - It sums the dues of claims whose **due-by** is in the period and that pass `countsAsOf`. That is the status from the claim log at the end of the period's last day; a hold takes out only claims still open and unbound now.
- **Closing**: `close` / `softClose` freezes `personTotals` and `closedTotal`.
  - Hard-closed: no changes at all to claims whose due-by falls in the period.
  - Soft-closed: changes are still allowed, but new claims are flagged as late entries.
  - `reopen` needs the `reopen` permission (steward only by the standing rule).
- **Auto-close** (`AutoClosePeriods`): when today changes and `grace-days` is set, it closes every open, not-soft-closed period whose to-date + grace is before today. The audit line ends `auto=yes`.
- **Generating** (`GeneratePeriods`, `GenerateFiscalYear`): one period per month named `yyyy-mm`, skipping months whose name or days are already taken. `period-fy` shows the fiscal year from `fiscal-start-month`.

### Rates, imports, paste and other bulk inputs
- **Rates** (`RateRules`): grade A, B or C; a percent ≥ 0 with two decimals; optional from- and to-dates.
  - Setting a rate replaces the one with the same from-date. `rate-current-<g>` falls back to the parent sheets.
  - **Rate preview**: counts how many OPEN or PENDING unbound claims would show a different due, and the sum of the differences.
- **Import people**: all-or-nothing. A line matching an existing name or alias updates that person, with the grade recorded from today.
- **Import rates**: all-or-nothing, each line handled exactly as the rate form would.
- **Paste claims**: all-or-nothing DRAFT claims, matched to people by name or alias, with `#ref` taken from the end of the note.
- **Quick-add**: adds a missing person with grade A. It checks the closed-period rule before adding anyone.
- **Plans** (`GeneratePlans`): makes DRAFT claims for plan dates up to today; refused dates are retried next time.
- **Bulk settle**: all-or-nothing (`CheckClaimSettle` dry-runs every claim first) and gets a batch number.
- **Pools** (`RespondWithPools`):
  - A pool's pot is the sheet's `pot`, or its cut in its parent pool.
  - Each cut is pot × share / (the sum of the shares that get a cut), rounded HALF_EVEN.
  - Retired members, members held on today, and members whose dates don't include today get no cut. The remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut, the latest-added member on a tie.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

Moderately hard. Most of the figure logic is in one well-commented class, `ClaimFigures`, but it is **written twice**: once in Java for settling, closing, statements and the audit file, and again in TypeScript (`rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `due.slot.tsx`, `periods.ts`, plus about a dozen slot files). What the screen shows comes from the TypeScript copy. Meanwhile the "who may do what", closed-period and retirement rules are repeated inline across roughly fifteen `Apply*` step classes. A new developer would have to keep both copies, and those scattered checks, in step by hand.

There are already small differences that show the cost:
- The `periods.slot.tsx` header comment says "date falls in it", but the code uses the due-by.
- A blank date on the claim form defaults to the entry date when adding, but to today when editing.
- In `Period.java`, the javadoc for `closedTotal` sits above `cap`.
